events.title: The CEO meeting starts in 23 minutes
events.body:
Welcome aboard. I have twenty-three minutes and one question: what are the three cyber risks I should be most concerned about?

You have inherited 6,283 critical vulnerabilities, 17 high-priority audit findings, 23 open risk register entries, four transformation programmes, fourteen important suppliers and five security vacancies.

Where do you start?

events.title: Your three risks
events.body: You have had one morning. I have five minutes. Tell me what you have.

events.title: Your leadership team
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body:
Four of us report to you. Between us we run security operations, incident response, architecture, engineering, identity, and cyber risk and governance.

A warning before you start assigning work. Everyone here is already committed. If you give us more, something else stops, or it comes back thinner than you wanted. We would rather you chose than we quietly disappointed you.

events.title: The inherited risk register
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body:
Twenty-three open entries. Nineteen have not been updated in eighteen months. Several describe systems that have since been decommissioned, and at least two describe controls that were subsequently switched off.

I would not read it as a description of where we are. I would read it as a description of what somebody was worried about in 2024.

events.title: Sign-off requested: new customer platform
events.body:
We are on track for launch and I need your sign-off in the pack. The date is public, the marketing spend is committed, and the board has been told.

I am not expecting a problem. If there is one, I need to know this week, not the week before launch.

events.title: External audit: privileged access, third year running
events.body:
The auditors have raised privileged access management again. That is three consecutive years, and the audit committee has noticed.

I need a response from you for the committee papers. Please do not send me the same remediation plan we sent last year.

events.title: SOC contract renewal decision required
events.from: Nadia Farrell, Director of Procurement and Supplier Management
events.body: Sentinel's contract renews in eight weeks and I need a direction from you. Renewing as-is is straightforward. Anything else takes time I need to start spending now.

events.title: Kestrel integration: network join scheduled
events.body:
Completion is confirmed. Integration have scheduled the network join for day one, as planned since February.

I understand you have views. I would rather hear them now than at the steering committee.

events.title: Cost programme: contribution requested
events.body:
The cost reduction programme is short. Every function is being asked to contribute and I am asking you for £220k of the cyber budget, or a named line worth half of it.

If the answer is no, I need to be able to explain to the executive what we lose.

events.title: Annual penetration test: scope decision
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: The testers want scope confirmed. Last year's engagement excluded the legacy data centre on cost grounds, which is convenient given it is the part I understand least.

events.title: The warehouse platform question
events.body:
I am told the Meridian platform is running on software that is no longer supported. I am also told it cannot be upgraded and that migration is at least a year away.

Despatch runs on it. Three sites. If it stops, we stop. What are you proposing to do about that?

events.title: First quarter closes
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body:
You have had a quarter. At the next committee I would like to hear what you now believe, what you have changed your mind about, and what you still cannot answer.

I am more interested in the third of those than the first two.

events.title: Your first year review
events.body:
Your first year is nearly up. I will want to talk about what changed, what you chose not to do, and whether we are in better shape than we were.

Bring the honest version.

events.title: Executive exception requests
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body:
Three executive assistants hold delegated access to their principals' mail and files, and the new privileged access flow now covers it. They cannot work with it, and their principals have asked to be exempted.

This is the point where the control either applies to everyone or quietly stops meaning anything.
